summary.oneLiner: The deck positions Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (formerly Amara Raja Batteries) as one of India's largest lead-acid battery makers with leading automotive and telecom/data-centre franchises, now redeploying its cash generation into an INR 95 Bn New Energy "Giga Corridor" in Telangana to lead India's energy transition.
summary.business: ARE&M manufactures automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries under brands like Amaron and Quanta, and is expanding into new energy through lithium-ion cell and pack manufacturing, EV charging, and battery recycling. The company serves OEMs, aftermarket customers, and infrastructure developers across over 70 countries, with a growing focus on energy storage systems and advanced cell technologies.

currentContext.strengths: Established brand leadership in lead-acid batteries with strong distribution network across India and presence in 70+ countries.|Vertically integrated operations through subsidiary ARCS for battery recycling, securing lead and alloy supply.|Diversifying into new energy with integrated platform spanning cell manufacturing, pack assembly, energy storage, and EV charging.|Long-standing technology partnerships and in-house R&D for advanced lead-acid and lithium-ion technologies.
currentContext.strategies: Strengthening governance practices through periodic auditor rotation and adoption of an Internal Audit Charter to enhance risk management, internal controls, and governance processes.|Inculcating a culture of risk management across the organization through extensive training and awareness sessions for employees.|Conducting CSR activities in education, health, environment, and rural development through Rajanna Foundation and Amara Raja Educational Society.|Disciplined capital allocation framework balancing investments across established Lead Acid Battery business and emerging New Energy operations, while maintaining a prudent balance sheet and funding flexibility. Capital directed towards manufacturing capacity, recycling infrastructure, cell development capabilities, energy storage solutions and research facilities, with shareholder distributions alongside business investments.|ARCS is establishing a state-of-the-art battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu, with de-sulphurisation technology (first-of-its-kind in India) to improve lead recovery yields, reduce waste, and produce Sodium Sulphate as a by-product.|ARACT's e+ Energy Labs in Hyderabad is being completed as an integrated research and innovation hub for advanced battery technologies.|The Company conducts CSR activities through Rajanna Foundation and Amara Raja Educational Society in education, health, environment, and rural development, with impact assessments undertaken for eligible projects.|The Company has adopted an Internal Audit Charter to strengthen risk management, internal controls, and governance processes.|The Company has a Whistle Blower Policy/Vigil Mechanism providing a safe and confidential platform for stakeholders to report concerns, including anonymous complaints.
currentContext.expansion: Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private Limited (ARCS), a wholly owned subsidiary, is establishing a battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu. Battery Breaker operations commenced during the year and are in ramp-up. Refining operations, which started in H2 2024, continue to scale up. Phase II refinery expansion is underway with commissioning targeted by 2027. Commissioning of the Crystallizer and De-sulphurisation plant is expected shortly. Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited (ARACT) is progressing its lithium-ion cell and battery pack manufacturing capabilities. The Pack Assembly Plant is ramping up towards a targeted annual supply capacity of 1.5 GWh. The Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) with cylindrical and prismatic cell manufacturing lines is in the process of commissioning. Construction at the Amara Raja Giga Corridor in Divitipally, Telangana, progressed substantially, with structural development and procurement of key process equipment advancing. Start of Production (SoP) for lithium-ion cell manufacturing is planned for 2027.

risks.risk: Execution risk in scaling new lithium-ion cell manufacturing
risks.note: ARACT is in early-stage ramp-up with net losses, targeting Start of Production by 2027; delays or cost overruns at the Giga Corridor could impact the strategic pivot to New Energy.

Shift from lead-acid to lithium-ion and advanced chemistries (LFP, NMC) exposes the company to technology risk, customer qualification delays, and potential stranded assets in legacy battery segments.

risks.risk: Raw material supply and circular-economy integration
risks.note: ARCS recycling ramp-up (Phase II refinery, de-sulphurisation) is critical for lead and alloy security. Delays in scaling refining or alloy production could disrupt cost and supply-chain resilience.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk in battery waste management
risks.note: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, and evolving environmental norms require continuous investment and operational adaptation, especially for recycling and lead operations.
Automotive and industrial battery segments rely on a concentrated OEM customer base; shifts in OEM procurement strategies or EV adoption rates could materially affect volumes and margins.
Increasing digitalisation across manufacturing, R&D, and customer interfaces elevates exposure to cyber threats, which could disrupt operations or compromise sensitive data.

The company is exposed to tightening climate regulations, carbon pricing, and investor expectations. Failure to meet SBTi or GHG reduction targets could lead to reputational damage and higher cost of capital.

one-line thesis: Amara Raja is pivoting from pure lead-acid dominance to integrated lithium cell manufacturing and BESS, with Q4FY26 showing resilient 15% revenue growth despite raw material inflation. The strategic shift to captive cell production (Giga 1 by Jun-27) and ESS integration aims to capture India's storage boom, though near-term margins are pressured by lead/alloy costs and high OEM mix.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 3,530cr (+15% YoY); EBITDA Margin 11% consolidated (12.3% adj. Lead Acid); PAT includes exceptional insurance claim net of gratuity one-off; Order Book not disclosed (project-based BESS); Net Debt not explicitly stated but capex funded via internal accruals and prior equity infusion.
guidance: FY27 Revenue: Mid-to-high single digit (Lead Acid); Margin: Targeting 13-14% long-term (currently 11-12%); Order Inflow: Strong telecom/ESS pipeline; Capex: INR 1,500-1,700cr (INR 1,100-1,200cr New Energy).
order book & pipeline: No formal backlog disclosed; BESS strategy relies on self-offtake and anticipated government localization mandates rather than binding long-term contracts.
segment / subsidiary detail: Lead Acid (92% rev): 4W OEM +30%, Aftermarket +5-6%, Tubular +35% (70-75% in-house); New Energy (8% rev): INR 280cr, 300MWh telecom packs supplied, 1GWh cumulative installed.
growth verticals / optionality: 16-20GWh cell capacity target; 5-10GWh ESS integration facility by end-CY26; Expansion into 4W OEM lithium programs; Auxiliary battery demand in hybrids.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material pressure: Lead/Alloys (70% basket) up due to geopolitics; Plastics (10% basket) +40% potential increase; Price hike of 5-6% taken in Q4, another 2-3% expected; Recycling accretion ~0.5%.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR 600cr total (INR 500cr net Lead Acid); FY27 Guidance: INR 1,500-1,700cr (INR 400cr Lead Acid, INR 1,100-1,200cr New Energy including Giga 1 and ESS plant).
capital allocation: INR 100cr infused into AR Advanced Cell Technologies in Q4 (total INR 1,500cr invested); Focus on R&D lab commissioning and pilot line stabilization.
risks & watch-items: Chinese technology licensing restrictions (Gotion deal stalled); Import cost disadvantage (China +15-20%); Lead price volatility; Slower EV adoption if localization mandates raise system costs.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes resilience, self-reliance in tech, and 'China+1' opportunity; Acknowledges cost headwinds but confident in pricing power and volume growth.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly states they will not be cost-competitive with Chinese imports initially (15-20% gap), betting entirely on government localization mandates (ALMM-style) for utility BESS to bridge the gap; Shift from EV-centric to ESS-centric near-term growth.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising lead and alloy costs squeezing margins across the sector | Exide Industries | beneficiary | Med | Peer likely facing similar cost pressures but may benefit from industry-wide price hikes if Amara Raja leads with 2-3% increase. |
| Government mandates for domestic content in BESS favor local integrators | Tata Power | beneficiary | Low | Potential partner or competitor in BESS space; policy tailwinds benefit all domestic integrators. |
| Import restrictions on Chinese cells could delay projects | Pure-play BESS Importers | loser | High | Entities relying solely on imported Chinese cells without domestic integration capabilities will face margin compression or disqualification from government tenders. |

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

themes.title: EV-OEM & domestic cell manufacturing
themes.need: Domestic EV OEMs and cell/Gigafactory localization (PLI) are scaling unit volumes and chasing battery cost-downs to reach profitability. The binding question is cell-to-pack localization and vehicle-volume ramp, distinct from Tier-1 component supply.
themes.driver: Vehicle-volume ramp + Gigafactory/PLI cell localization & improving EV-OEM unit economics.
